Subject: RE: Quick usage review ahead of renewal

Emma — thanks for the note. I pulled together a short summary and attached the Q2 usage spreadsheet. High level:

- What happened: A backend validation job was accidentally left in debug mode (doubled prompt length) between 2027-05-04 02:00 UTC and 2027-05-06 19:30 UTC, causing a ~3.7x increase in tokens per inference for that job. The job accounted for ~42% of the daily burn on peak day.

- Performance & ROI impact: latency was stable (99th p95 within 1.2x baseline) thanks to warm KV-caching and continuous batching. Unit cost increased only because prompt length rose — the runtime amortized GPU compute effectively. Estimated incremental spend for the incident: ~$18.4k over three days (see q2-usage-report.xlsx).

- Short-term remediation options:
  1) Burst-ladder (recommended): 30% burst credits for 30 days, capped daily, billed as blended overage at a reduced premium. Avoids moving to a permanent higher commit.
  2) Temporary tier bump: +20% committed capacity for two quarters — lowers unit cost but upfront commit.
  3) Prompt/ops controls: deploy guardrails and a pre-deploy token regression check in CI — low cost, medium effort.

- Proposal: We recommend the Burst-ladder pilot + a prompt regression check. Details: 60k token/day burst credit for 30 days, automatic fallback to standard capacity after cap. I'll attach an SLA draft that includes burst-ladder caps and response escalation.

Next steps I suggest: 1) You confirm whether procurement wants the burst-ladder included as part of renewal paperwork, 2) if yes, we produce a short DocuSign amendment and a 1-page explanation for your procurement folder.

I attached: q2-usage-report.xlsx (per-day token burn + job breakdown) and sla-burst-ladder-draft.pdf.

Happy to jump on a 20' call if you want to walk the numbers.

Best,

Michael Grant

Adding some ops context — Emma, quick points that help procurement decide:

- SLA & latency: we can commit the same latency SLOs for the burst-ladder window; burst traffic will be routed to reserved warm pools to preserve p95.
- Cost mechanics: burst-ladder is structured as a timeboxed, capped overage. Price: +25% blended premium over standard per-token rate for burst consumption. We can show a modeled blended rate in the HubSpot deal (link below).
- Risk controls: we’ll set automatic throttles per job and add a preflight token-length validator so accidental debug configs don't spike costs again.

If procurement prefers a commit instead of burst credits, the equivalent economics for a 2-quarter +20% commit looks like a ~10% reduction in per-token rate but requires the committed spend. I put both options in the draft DocuSign language and the HubSpot deal notes.

Link to deal & model: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/7890123

If you’re comfortable, Michael, I can push the DocuSign with the burst-ladder amendment for signature and add the usage one-pager to the package.

—Ben
